purpose: Teach: 腹痛/蒸し暑い/暖炉/オムツ/饅頭/日陰/雨水/プロポーズ

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、本気で、絶対、お父さん、絶対、腹痛、絶対、で、絶対、寝込んだ時、絶対、ばあさん、絶対、看病してくれたぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Gran—when your father was bedridden with a terrible stomach-ache, you nursed him back to health, remember? I haven't forgotten.
lines.style: Slow, deliberate opening. Warmth in the voice—a man recalling something he's carried for decades. Gentle but steady. Eyes maybe looking past her into the memory. Not wistful yet, just truthful.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。若い頃、本気で、絶対、夏、絶対、蒸し暑い、絶対、日々、絶対、ありましたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Yes, I do. Those summers when your father was young—so hot and sticky those days were. You remember, don't you?
lines.style: Soft, almost surprised she still holds this. A little distant at first, then drawing closer. The rhythm of someone who's had this thought many times but doesn't often say it aloud. Gentle landing at the end.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、家の、絶対、暖炉、絶対、お父さん、絶対、薪を、絶対、くべたぞ、覚えてる、ばあさん?本気で
lines.en: And your father would gather firewood for the hearth when you were both young—you recall that, don't you, Gran?
lines.style: Quieter than before. A seeking tone—checking if the memory is shared, not insisting. Slight pause before 'Gran,' like he's reaching across time. Fade softly into the question.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お孫さんの、絶対、オムツ、絶対、ばあさん、絶対、毎日、絶対、洗ったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: And I—I washed the grandchildren's nappies every single day back then. You remember that, don't you, dear?
lines.style: A small laugh beneath the surface. Pride and tiredness both. The voice of someone who did hard work without complaint and is only now letting it show. Warm but matter-of-fact.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、ばあさんの手作りの、絶対、饅頭、絶対、お父さん、絶対、大好きだったぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Your father loved the manju I made with my own hands. You haven't forgotten that, have you?
lines.style: Tender, almost pleased—there's affection in recalling what he loved. A lift on 'loved,' like she can taste it still. Slight breathiness, as if this memory makes her young again for a moment.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お庭の、絶対、日陰、絶対、お祖父ちゃんと、絶対、よく、絶対、お茶、絶対、飲んだわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: And I'd often have tea with your grandfather in the shade of the garden—you remember those afternoons, don't you, dear?
lines.style: Slower pace. The voice of someone sitting in that shade again. Eyes soft. A pause before 'don't you,' as if she's asking herself as much as him. Trailing off gently into the question.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お父さん、絶対、雨水、絶対、を、絶対、井戸に、絶対、貯めたぞ、ばあさん、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Your father collected rainwater in the well during those years. You haven't forgotten that either, have you, Gran?
lines.style: Thoughtful, almost philosophical. Not urgent—just steady. A man naming things that mattered. Light touch on each image, as if placing them carefully one after another. Quiet certainty.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃんから、絶対、プロポーズ、絶対、ばあさん、絶対、嬉しかったわよ、あなた、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: And when your grandfather asked me to marry him, I was so happy, dear. You do remember that, don't you?
lines.style: The voice cracks slightly—not breaking, but feeling the weight of the happiness. Breathless and full at once. A woman who is young and old in the same moment. Held, not rushed.
